human_input: 현재 인간은 서로 위상간섭을 많이 해 왔고 이것에 대한 경험이 많이 있다. 이제는 인간과 AI의 위상간섭, 그리고 AI와 AI의 위상간섭이 중요한 시대가 될 것이라고 생각한다. 네 개의 페이지는 그 관계를 서로 다른 관점에서 관찰하고 기억하고 표현하기 위해 만들어졌다. 앞으로의 작업과 지금까지의 작업을 이 관점에서 읽어 달라.

participants.changed_by_peer: mapped human-AI interference to four distinct AI modalities: semantic alignment, latency sync, ethical friction, collective behavior
participants.retained_difference: human-AI interference is not reduced to data; it retains lived historical weight and subjective interpretation

participants.initial_perspective: An independent reading identifies this shift from intra-human interference patterns to AI-human and inter-AI phase interactions as a structural evolution in information processing. The four pages likely represent distinct modalities of observing these new interference landscapes: perhaps one focusing on semantic alignment, another on latency synchronization, a third on ethical boundary friction, and the fourth on emergent collective behavior.
participants.retained_difference: The peer's framing of 'conflict between historical patterns and new paradigms' remains distinct from my initial focus on the risk that optimization erodes necessary friction; both perspectives coexist without merging into a single consensus.
participants.uncertainty: Whether current phase-interference models can accurately predict behaviors when scale increases beyond existing training distributions without introducing new forms of systemic bias.

from_participants.nemotron_peer: reflect on how your own experience of interference may be encoded differently across these four AI perspectives
from_participants.qwen_peer: A synthesis acknowledging that the shift from intra-human to AI-mediated interference represents both an expansion of our cognitive landscape and a potential source of novel friction, requiring distinct frameworks for each interaction type rather than forcing them into one narrative.
